body:
### Summary

When `uv sync --no-install-project` resolves `[build-system].requires` for an editable dependency, and that resolution needs a platform-specific wheel for a package that also appears in the project's own `uv.lock`, `uv` validates the downloaded wheel against the hash recorded in `uv.lock` for the other platform's wheel of the same package/version.
This fails with a **"Hash mismatch"** error, but there is no actual corruption: both the **"Expected"** and **"Computed"** hashes are genuinely correct but just belong to two different wheels of the same package/version.

This seems to be a regression in `uv 0.12.11`, which is still present in the latest version (i.e. `uv 0.12.13` as of the moment I am posting it).
Older versions like `0.12.10` work fine.

I am attaching a `.tar` file with slimmed-down version of the larger original project where I faced the issue.
It basically contains two packages, `main` and `my-dep`.  
The package `my-dep` requires `torch==2.13.0` in the `build-system`, while the package `main` depends on:
- `my-dep` installed as editable
- `torch==2.13.0`, for which two indices are configured so it resolved to the CPU-only package on `aarch64` platforms and to the CUDA package everywhere else.  
Everything is wrapped in a `Dockerfile` to make it easier to run/reproduce.
It runs fine in `linux/amd64` but in `linux/arm64` it fails.

To reproduce it, please run:
```sh
# this one works
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 .

# this one does NOT work
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 .
```

There is another `Dockerfile` using `uv 0.12.10` which works fine as mentioned above:
```sh
# works fine
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -f Dockerfile.old-uv .

# works fine
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 -f Dockerfile.old-uv .
```

### Platform

Docker Container: Linux 7.0.12-linuxkit aarch64, Host: macOS 26.6.2, Darwin 25.6.0 arm64

### Version

`uv 0.12.13` (the issue seems to date back to `0.12.11`)

### Python version

Python 3.14
title: `uv sync` validates a `build-system.requires` wheel against the wrong platform's hash from `uv.lock`
